item.title: Finite-sample certification of coverage regret for budgeted document selection under adaptive stratified auditing
item.description: arXiv:2610.19207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Selecting a budget-constrained set of documentary fragments, for instance the knowledge base of a retrieval-augmented generation system, raises a statistical question: how much expected query coverage is lost relative to the best feasible selection when the query distribution is unknown? We construct finite-sample, distribution-free upper confidence bounds for this coverage regret that remain valid after data-dependent selection. A pilot stage may select the document set, screen competitors, build comparison networks and learn an annotation policy. Then an independent audit acquires relevance labels with probabilities that are constant within observable strata. The main result is a simultaneous bound for all retained coverage contrasts. The bound is made observable by empirical-Bernstein variance calibration or by a one-stage construction without calibration, and it accounts for estimated stratum proportions. For maximum-type coverage we prove variance contractions for swaps of redundant fragments, give a condition under which multiscale radii improve on a direct union bound, and show that such redundancy cannot be certified from samples alone. A simulation study confirms validity and quantifies the gains from variance calibration and certified redundancy.
item.dc:creator: Nora Serdyukova

item.title: Pointwise minimax lower bounds under a multi-index constraint: the price of an unknown orientation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider nonparametric regression with random design and non-Gaussian noise, where the regression function has the multi-index form $F(x)=f(\Theta x)$ with an unknown link $f:\RR^m\to\RR$ in an anisotropic H\"older class and an unknown matrix $\Theta$ with $m\le d$ orthonormal rows. For estimation of $F$ at a fixed point we prove that the minimax risk is bounded from below by a multiple of $L^{1/(2\gamma+1)}(n^{-1}\ln n)^{\gamma/(2\gamma+1)}$, where $\gamma$ is the harmonic mean of the smoothness indices of the link divided by $m$. For $m<d$ this extends a Gaussian white noise result to regression. The main new case is $m=d$, where no dimension reduction takes place: the logarithmic factor still appears as soon as the link is anisotropic and the orientation of its axes is unknown. In contrast, when the link is isotropic with smoothness index at most one, the class is rotation invariant up to a constant and the classical rate without logarithm is attained. The logarithmic loss is therefore caused by the unknown orientation of the directions in which the function is least smooth
item.dc:creator: Nora Serdyukova

item.title: On Local Inference for Functionals of Ill-Posed Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.19350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study inference for continuous linear functionals of solutions to ill-posed inverse problems, including Euclidean parameters arising in nonparametric instrumental variables, proximal causal inference, and shadow-variable models. Although pointwise root-$n$ inference is possible under standard conditions, we show that this need not translate into locally reliable inference. Under a model imposing only minimal regularity conditions, the target is Hellinger discontinuous when both inverse problems are ill-posed: arbitrarily small changes in the data-generating law can produce arbitrarily large changes in the target, ruling out informative locally uniform inference. Imposing a uniform bound on a minimum-norm solution restores Hellinger continuity under regularity conditions, but does not by itself ensure stable root-n inference. If, in addition, both inverse problems are ill-posed and the solution whose norm is uniformly bounded is nonunique at a law $P_0$, then under regularity conditions the target fails to be pathwise differentiable; consequently, asymptotically linear estimators exhibit nonvanishing root-$n$ bias under some local alternatives, causing Wald confidence intervals to undercover asymptotically. Under regularity conditions, pathwise differentiability is restored if the uniformly bounded solution is unique at $P_0$. It is also restored, regardless of uniqueness, under the stronger requirement that the corresponding solution satisfy a uniformly bounded $\beta$-source condition for some $\beta$>0. We relate these regimes to very weak, weak, and strong identification in instrumental variables models.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Graham, Andrea Rotnitzky

item.title: Softplus Affine(1, 1) Processes: Enlarged Stationarity Region, Stationary Unit Roots, and Inference
item.description: arXiv:2610.19421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Softplus affine\((1,1)\) models keep the conditional mean positive while allowing coefficients of either sign. We study them under Poisson, negative binomial, gamma and related conditional distributions. A stationary solution with moments of all positive orders exists whenever the coefficient sum is less than one, strictly enlarging previously known sufficient regions. At the unit root, the coefficient sum equals one. Under an invertibility condition, a stationary solution exists in this case if and only if the intercept is negative. At a stationary unit root, the conditional mean has a power-law tail with an explicit index, and the observations can exhibit long memory. For a fixed softplus scale, the Poisson quasi-maximum likelihood estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal at the usual \(\sqrt n\) rate below and at the unit root, with the coefficient sum left unrestricted in estimation. At the unit root, these results require only a finite mean and yield standard Wald inference even when the observations have infinite variance or long memory. Simulations and two applications examine finite-sample inference and sensitivity to the softplus scale.
item.dc:creator: Yang Lu, Fukang Zhu

item.title: A New Perspective on Cumulative Residual R\'enyi Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2610.19903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a new cumulative residual R\'enyi entropy (CRRE), which addresses limitations of the existing cumulative residual R\'enyi entropy. The conventional measure suffers from two primary drawbacks: its failure to converge to the cumulative residual entropy (CRE) as the order parameter approaches unity, and its lack of guaranteed positivity. Our proposed CRRE resolves these issues, offering a theoretically consistent and always nonnegative measure of uncertainty in residual lifetimes. We explore its mathematical properties, including its relationship with existing information measures. Furthermore, the concept is extended to its dynamic version, and its time-dependent characteristics are investigated. A non-parametric estimator of the proposed CRRE is developed, its almost sure convergence is established, and is validated through Monte Carlo simulation. The effectiveness of CRRE as a tool for quantifying uncertainty is confirmed through its application in chaotic theory and financial data.
item.dc:creator: Shubham Babasaheb Alte, Swaroop Georgy Zachariah, Mohd. Arshad

item.title: Drift parameter estimation for interacting particle systems with singular repulsion
item.description: arXiv:2610.20090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the estimation of the interaction parameter in singular interacting particle systems from continuous and discrete observations over a fixed time horizon. The singularity of the interaction drift prevents the direct application of standard likelihood and contrast-based methods, which rely on regularity assumptions that fail in this setting. Our approach exploits an exact reduction of the particle dynamics to a one-dimensional stochastic differential equation for a quadratic empirical moment. By the symmetry of the interaction kernel, the singular terms cancel, yielding an explicit estimator in which the unknown parameter enters linearly. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality as the number of particles, \(N\), tends to infinity. Letting \(\varepsilon_N\) denote the microscopic noise scaling of the system, we obtain asymptotic normality at the rate \(\sqrt{N/\varepsilon_N}\) for strictly positive interaction kernels, under an additional condition on the limiting empirical information. We further extend these results to degenerate interaction kernels, achieving consistency and asymptotic normality at rate \(N\) under suitable structural assumptions and the canonical scaling \(\varepsilon_N=N^{-1}\). In both regimes, we provide conditions on the observation mesh ensuring that the statistical limits remain valid under discrete sampling, in high frequency. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of our methodology through Dyson Brownian motion, the Dyson Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, and Wishart--Laguerre particle systems, alongside a numerical investigation of the estimators' finite-sample performance.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Amorino, Jacek Malecki, Radomyra Shevchenko

item.title: On rigidity of infinite exchangeable sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.18992v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We ask when the law of an infinite exchangeable sequence is uniquely determined by a finite-dimensional marginal. For mixtures of a probability kernel, a weak localization condition makes three coordinates determine the directing law. Completeness alone makes four coordinates sufficient. Neither order can be lowered in general. For exponential kernels with a nonnegative sufficient statistic, a M\"untz-Sz\'asz support condition implies three coordinates suffice. In the scalar case, this result is sharp. We also characterize when completeness holds simultaneously for all scalar mixing laws by a weighted M\"untz density condition and show that statistic support alone need not decide completeness. These methods yield sharp finite-dimensional refinements of Freedman's theorem on rotatable sequences, namely that spherical symmetry of three coordinates makes an infinite exchangeable sequence rotatable while symmetry of the first two coordinates is in general insufficient. Finally, for energy-radial densities we give a complete-monotonicity criterion for infinite extendibility and determine the exact uniqueness thresholds for $\ell_q$-norm exponential laws.
item.dc:creator: Maximillian Newman

item.title: Asymptotic Behavior of Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2610.19358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study the behavior of transformer networks generating text over long periods of time. We show that even a three-token, single-layer attention-only transformer can fail to converge. We then study a rich class of transformers with arbitrary finite depth, layer normalization, MLPs, RoPE encodings, and an arbitrary mix of local and global layers. Every transformer in this class has a softmax temperature threshold above which its empirical cache distribution converges to a unique limit, independent of initial conditions. We show further that, while each transformer has a temperature threshold, the supremum of this set is infinite, so there is no global minimal temperature that forces all transformers to converge.
item.dc:creator: Katy Blumer, Da-Cheng Juan, Jon Kleinberg, Ravi Kumar, Cyrus Rashtchian, Andrew Tomkins

item.title: On Inherent Privacy of Posterior Sampling: A Unified R\'enyi-Divergence Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.19573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Differential Privacy (DP) provides a rigorous framework for quantifying privacy guarantees. While most methods achieve DP by injecting calibrated random noise, the intrinsic randomness of certain procedures such as sampling can yield DP guarantees ``for free''. In this work, we develop a unified R\'enyi divergence framework to characterize the inherent DP guarantees of sampling from a Bayesian posterior distribution. We show that the privacy loss incurred by One-Posterior-Sampling (OPS) is governed by posterior exponential moments of the single-record log-likelihood ratio, and establish explicit DP guarantees under uniformly bounded, sub-Gaussian, or sub-exponential tail regimes. We apply the framework to representative Bayesian models, including categorical likelihoods with arbitrary priors, Gaussian-Gaussian conjugate pair, generalized linear models from the exponential family and linear regression with Gaussian likelihood, both with Gaussian priors on the regression coefficients. Our results elucidate sample size, model structure, neighboring relations in DP (bounded or unbounded), and how prior if applicable, jointly determine the inherent DP guarantees of OPS. Furthermore, our results recover the existing DP guarantees for OPS as special cases -- often with tighter privacy loss bounds -- and substantially broaden the class of Bayesian models for which the inherent DP guarantees of OPS can be rigorously characterized.
item.dc:creator: Ruyu Zhou, Fang Liu

item.title: Model-Induced Hazard Geometry and Functional Representations in Survival Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.19643v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Individualized survival predictions are often summarized by scalar risk scores or event probabilities at selected time horizons, although clinically relevant risk may also differ in its temporal organization. We consider finite-dimensional representations of individual hazard trajectories through interpretable hazard functionals, such as peak timing, cumulative hazard over prespecified intervals, and persistence of elevated risk. A central issue is that the richness of such representations is constrained by the hazard geometry supported by the underlying survival model. We formalize this through model-induced tangent spaces and functional ranks, derive an exact decomposition of model-supported variation into directions retained and lost by a chosen representation, and introduce a model-relative notion of local completeness. We further distinguish intrinsic model capacity from the variation actually activated by covariates. These results motivate a structured extension of AFT time scaling through a positive-affine deformation on the log-time scale, yielding a power-warp mechanism with an additional temporal deformation direction. Combined with a log-logistic reference hazard, this gives a parsimonious likelihood-based working specification for which peak timing and peak height provide complete coordinates over the unimodal regime. We also establish plug-in recovery and asymptotic inference for hazard functionals. Simulations and a lung-cancer application illustrate how model-induced restrictions propagate to hazard-functional representations.
item.dc:creator: Xijia Liu

item.title: Maximum Likelihood Degrees via One-Edge Chordal Completion
item.description: arXiv:2610.19669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The maximum likelihood degree of a Gaussian graphical model measures the algebraic complexity of its likelihood equations. This paper studies maximum likelihood degrees of Gaussian graphical models through chordal completion. When a graph becomes chordal after one missing edge is added, its maximum likelihood degree is determined by the maximal cliques and clique-tree separators containing that edge. This recovers Uhler's formula for complete bipartite graphs with one part of size two, and extends it to deleted-spine clique books, whose degree is unchanged when a page is thickened to a clique. For several fill edges, the same method gives a product formula when no clique or separator bag contains two fill edges. We also determine four classes of vertices at which clique blow-up preserves the degree. Two follow from known results, and two are established here.
item.dc:creator: Nilava Metya

item.title: Minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap of continuous Markov chains, with applications to empirical concentration bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.20007v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap $\gamma_{ps}$ of a Markov chain from the observation of a single trajectory. Extending earlier works on finite-state space chains by Wolfer and Kontorovich (2024), we provide an estimator in the case of a compact, continuous state-space. Our estimator appears to be minimax-optimal on the class of chains with a transition operator with Lipschitz density, up to logarithmic terms. Our estimator, combined with Paulin's version of Bernstein inequality, allows to derive empirical concentration inequalities for Markov chains. This unlocks many applications, from confidence intervals, to active learning and generalization bounds. In particular, for rested bandits with Markov rewards, we provide a version of UCB with a regret bound similar to the one in the iid case, without assuming any knowledge on the pseudo-spectral gap of the chains.
item.dc:creator: Vahe Karagulyan, Miko{\l}aj Kasprzak, Pierre Alquier

item.title: MCMC Can See Can't See
item.description: arXiv:2610.20020v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is folklore that passing "convergence" diagnostics does not guarantee that a Markov chain has converged. We prove this as an impossibility for any finite checklist of diagnostics. Running more chains, longer chains, and smarter diagnostics does not avoid this impossibility in certifying convergence. Under regularity assumptions, we determine how the worst-case undetected non-convergence decays as more diagnostics are added, and how to choose diagnostics optimally. Folklore suggests that the sampler's slowest mixing modes are the "dangerous" ones that must be monitored; we prove that the slow modes yield nearly optimal diagnostics as sampling proceeds. Given a source class, we also give an anytime-valid bound on the remaining discrepancy and show how undetected bias caps the effective sample size that a finite checklist can certify.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Matsui Smola

item.title: Monitoring for a Phase Transition in a Time Series of Wigner Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2507.04983v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop methodology and theory for the detection of a phase transition in a time-series of high-dimensional random matrices. In the model we study, at each time point \( t = 1,2,\ldots \), we observe a deformed Wigner matrix \( \mathbf{M}_t \), where the unobservable deformation represents a latent signal. This signal is detectable only in the supercritical regime, and our objective is to detect the transition to this regime in real time, as new matrix--valued observations arrive. Our approach is based on a partial sum process of extremal eigenvalues of $\mathbf{M}_t$, and its theoretical analysis combines state-of-the-art tools from random-matrix-theory and Gaussian approximations. The resulting detector is self-normalized, which ensures appropriate scaling for convergence and a pivotal limit, without any additional parameter estimation. Simulations show excellent performance for varying dimensions. Applications to pollution monitoring and social interactions in primates illustrate the usefulness of our approach.
item.dc:creator: Nina D\"ornemann, Piotr Kokoszka, Tim Kutta, Sunmin Lee

item.title: Random sets from the perspective of metric statistics
item.description: arXiv:2511.13440v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Since the seminal work by Beresteanu and Molinari(2008), the random set theory and related inference methods have been widely applied in partially identified econometric models. Meanwhile, there is an emerging field in statistics for studying random objects in metric spaces, called metric statistics. This paper clarifies a relationship between two fundamental concepts in these literatures, the Aumann and Fr\'echet means, and presents some applications of metric statistics to econometric problems involving random sets.
item.dc:creator: Daisuke Kurisu, Yuta Okamoto, Taisuke Otsu

item.title: Minimax Binary Counting under Shuffle Privacy: Poisson Limits and Randomized-Response Optimality
item.description: arXiv:2603.10073v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study estimation of a deterministic binary count from the shuffled outputs of a common single-message local channel. Privacy is required for every neighboring composition at fixed global parameters $(\varepsilon,\delta)$, and estimators may be biased. We obtain uniform critical Poisson and Skellam approximations and characterize the limiting minimax risk as an infimum over finite observed-mark Poisson experiments. Let $\Lambda$ be the noise intensity required by the boundary Poisson-shift profile and let $\lambda_{\min}$ be the intensity required by the full composition-maximized randomized-response profile. Binary randomized response is asymptotically minimax optimal if and only if $\Lambda=\lambda_{\min}$. When $\Lambda<\lambda_{\min}$, the minimax value lies strictly between $(\Lambda+\lambda_{\min})/2$ and $\lambda_{\min}$, and a randomized-response construction with observed rare marks strictly improves on binary randomized response. We give a finite-sample certified example. Binary randomized response is strictly suboptimal at $\varepsilon=0$ for every $0<\delta<1$, and this persists for sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$ at each fixed target. For every fixed positive $\varepsilon$, strict suboptimality also occurs along a sequence of fixed privacy targets tending to zero. The variational characterization permits approximation by finite marked channels; it does not assert that a finite optimizer exists.
item.dc:creator: Alex Shvets

item.title: Asymptotics for likelihood ratio tests of boundary points with singular information and unidentifiable nuisance parameters
item.description: arXiv:2605.08471v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the asymptotic distribution of likelihood ratio tests when nuisance parameters are unidentifiable under the null hypothesis, parameters of interest lie on the boundary, and the information matrix of the identifiable parameters may be singular. Mixture models, change point models and genetic linkage analysis exhibit all three features simultaneously. Under the null hypothesis the limit is the supremum of a chi-bar-squared process, whose marginal distributions are mixtures of chi-squared distributions with weights depending on the nuisance parameter; under local alternatives it is the supremum of a noncentral chi-bar-squared process. Unlike prior work on singular information, where singularity stems from the parameter of interest and changes the limit's form, here it occurs only at isolated values of the nuisance parameter, and under additional conditions the limit keeps its nonsingular form. Classical boundary results and application-specific results for mixtures, change points and linkage analysis are recovered and extended.
item.dc:creator: Karl Oskar Ekvall, Ola H\"ossjer, Matteo Bottai, J. M. Patrik Albin

item.title: A proximal gradient algorithm for composite log-concave sampling
item.description: arXiv:2605.12461v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an algorithm to sample from composite log-concave distributions over $\mathbb{R}^d$, i.e., densities of the form $\pi\propto e^{-f-g}$, assuming access to gradient evaluations of $\alpha_f$-convex $f$ and a restricted Gaussian oracle (RGO) for $\alpha_g$-convex $g$, where $\alpha_g \ge 0$. The latter requirement means that we can easily sample from the density $\text{RGO}_{g,h,y}(x) \propto \exp(-g(x) -\frac{1}{2h}||y-x||^2)$, which is the sampling analogue of the proximal operator for $g$. If $f + g$ is $\alpha$-convex and $f$ is $\beta$-smooth, our sampler achieves $\varepsilon$ error in total variation distance using $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\kappa \sqrt d \log^4(1/\varepsilon))$ oracle calls where $\kappa := 1 \vee \beta/\alpha$, with $0\le \alpha_g \le \beta$ and $\alpha := \alpha_f + \alpha_g > 0$, which matches prior state-of-the-art results for the case $g=0$. We further extend our results to cases where (1) $\pi$ is non-log-concave but satisfies a Poincar\'e or log-Sobolev inequality, and (2) $f$ is non-smooth but Lipschitz.
item.dc:creator: Linghai Liu, Sinho Chewi

item.title: The Zero Pattern of a Design Matrix Drives Multiple Descent in Over-parameterized Regression
item.description: arXiv:2607.24041v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Over-parameterized linear regression has been widely studied over the last decade. However, most existing works assume that the covariates are independent and that their covariance matrices are non-degenerate. In this paper, we relax both assumptions and derive deterministic equivalents for the prediction risk in a vanishing-ridge regime. We show that degeneracy of the covariance matrices and dependence can lead to multiple descent, and characterize where the corresponding peaks can occur. Our proofs use a novel graph representation of the variance profile. We show that maximum matchings and the Dulmage--Mendelsohn decomposition of the associated bipartite graph identify the configurations at which the variance becomes singular.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Han Huang, Haoyu Ye, Somak Laha, Morgane Austern

item.title: Asymptotics and finite sample bounds for prediction and smoothing in Wright-Fisher hidden Markov models
item.description: arXiv:2609.22444v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study signal prediction and smoothing in hidden Markov models whose latent signal is a multi-type Wright-Fisher diffusion and whose discrete-time observations are categorical. We consider a repeated-sampling regime with finitely many inspection times and large within-time samples. Under parent-independent mutation, the Bayesian predictive and smoothing laws admit exact representations as mixtures of Dirichlet distributions. We show that the one-step predictive and local smoothing laws converge in total variation to the corresponding Wright-Fisher transition and bridge laws determined by the neighboring population frequencies, thereby justifying plug-in approximations based on empirical proportions. For prediction, we derive explicit finite-sample bounds for this approximation and for bounded predictive functionals such as diversity, together with a finite-sample concentration bound for the marginal smoother. The joint posterior at the inspection times concentrates at the target frequencies and satisfies a Bernstein-von Mises limit with distinct interior and boundary regimes, with Gaussian and Gamma limits on different scales. The results allow arbitrary dependence across inspection times. A key technical ingredient is a fixed-interval tail bound for the coalescent-based dual death process.
item.dc:creator: Luigi M. Malgieri, Filippo Ascolani, Matteo Giordano, Matteo Ruggiero

item.title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with an RBF Kernel
item.description: arXiv:2610.10080v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gaussian processes (GPs) are widely used across machine learning, spatial statistics, time-series analysis, optimization, Bayesian statistics, and scientific applications. A central component of a GP model is its kernel, which is typically specified through a parametric family. Among the most widely used choices is the radial basis function (RBF), also known as the squared exponential or Gaussian kernel, owing to its simple form, smoothness, and flexibility. In practice, the kernel parameters are routinely estimated by the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs), as implemented by standard GP software. Despite this widespread use, the asymptotic behavior of the MLEs remains poorly understood under fixed-domain asymptotics, even for the RBF kernel. The main difficulty arises from the increasingly strong dependence among densely sampled observations and the nonlinear dependence of the covariance matrix on the kernel parameters. In this paper, we address this gap by providing, to the best of our knowledge, the first complete asymptotic characterization of the joint MLE of the spatial variance, lengthscale, and nugget variance under fixed-domain asymptotics. We establish consistency, derive convergence rates for all three parameters, prove joint asymptotic normality, and show that these rates are minimax optimal.
item.dc:creator: Ameer Qaqish, Sudipto Banerjee, Didong Li

item.title: Controlling the false discovery rate in high-dimensional linear models using model-X knockoffs and $p$-values
item.description: arXiv:2505.16124v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a novel multiple testing methodology for controlling the false discovery rate (FDR) in high-dimensional linear models that integrates model-X knockoff techniques with debiased penalized regression estimators. At the foundation of our methodology, we construct and study two sets of naturally paired high-dimensional test statistics and the associated $p$-values for evaluating the same null hypotheses. The first set is shown to be asymptotically mutually independent, justifying the use of the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. We further exploit the pairing structure through a two-step procedure aimed at improving power. Our theoretical results establish the key properties of the framework with respect to asymptotic FDR control and formally characterize the associated power gains of the two-step procedure. Importantly, our framework accommodates general dependence in the design matrix. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our methods outperform existing approaches -- particularly those relying on empirical FDP estimates -- in both power and FDR control accuracy, with notable gains in settings involving weaker signals, small sample sizes, or low target FDR levels.
item.dc:creator: Jinyuan Chang, Chenlong Li, Cheng Yong Tang, Zhengtian Zhu

item.title: Simulation Based Inference of a Simple Neural Network Structure
item.description: arXiv:2604.18599v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neurophysiologists are nowadays able to record from a large number of extracellular electrodes and to extract, from the raw data, the sequences of action potentials or spikes generated by many neurons. Unfortunately these ''many neurons'' still represent only a tiny fraction of the neuronal population that constitutes the network. Using association statistics such as the estimation of the cross-correlation functions, they are trying to infer the structure of the network formed by the recorded neurons. But this inference is compromised by the tremendous under-sampling of the neuronal population. We propose to focus instead on simple spike train statistics, like the empirical spikes frequency, or the interspike interval distribution. Their sampling distributions can be estimated by simulations, and, given a few observed spike train statistics, they provide enough information to infer the structure of the underlying network. We show that, on a ''toy model'', our method gives significantly better results than the sub-network reconstruction method with regards to the inference of the connection probability of the original network.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Charitat (IRMA), S\'egolen Geffray (IRMA), Christophe Pouzat (IRMA)

item.title: The Statistical Benefits of Multiple Responses for Learning from Demonstrations
item.description: arXiv:2609.33291v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many generative systems return multiple candidate responses and are evaluated according to the best one. Recent work shows that, when demonstrations are optimal, pass@$k$ can reduce the sample complexity of learning from demonstrations by a logarithmic factor in $k$. We ask what happens when the demonstrator is not assumed to be optimal. We find that multiple responses provide a qualitatively stronger benefit in this setting. In a finite reward-class model with no reward feedback, moving from pass@$1$ to any pass@$k$ with $k\ge2$ changes the worst-case dependence on target accuracy from $1/\varepsilon^2$ to $1/\varepsilon$, uniformly over demonstrator quality. Under standard evaluation, where an unknown reward is fixed before training, increasing $k$ provides an additional and distinct benefit: the optimal dependence on a reward class of size $N$ improves from $\log N$ to $\log N/\log k$. We further show that these two effects can be separated. Under robust evaluation, where one learned policy must compete with the demonstrator simultaneously for every reward in the class, the fast $1/\varepsilon$ dependence persists, while the $1/\log k$ improvement can disappear. We establish matching upper and lower bounds in the corresponding regimes and give a greedy multiplicative-weights learner achieving the upper bounds without any assumption on demonstrator quality.
item.dc:creator: Chandramauli Chakraborty, Cong Ma

item.title: Vine Copula VAR:From Recursive Margins to Joint Forecast Inference
item.description: arXiv:2610.07589v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Joint-event forecasts combine an estimated dependence model with current marginal forecasts. Retaining historical transforms at the marginal fits available when each outcome arrived creates overlapping estimation errors. We derive their joint influence with the terminal estimates in a stable Vine Copula VAR with normal innovation margins and a fixed, correctly specified Gaussian or positive Clayton vine. An intercept identity and the stable VAR filter reduce the historical correction to harmonically weighted innovation moments. Terminal slope uncertainty remains in the forecast gradient. A feasible covariance estimator yields asymptotically valid repeated-sample intervals for fixed one-sided event probabilities at the realized forecast state. A same-family terminal refit provides the efficiency comparison. Retaining dated transforms adds a positive semidefinite limiting covariance term, whose event-level cost depends on dependence sensitivity and forecast-state leverage. Monte Carlo comparisons show a small accuracy cost of retaining the transforms and a larger inferential role for current marginal estimation. Allowing Clayton dependence improves downside forecasts relative to Gaussian dependence under each transform rule. A fourteen-variable U.S. real-time forecasting application and simulations with twenty and fifty variables illustrate feasible joint-event estimation and analytic inference for fixed-depth vines.
item.dc:creator: Hunter Ng, Yubo Tao
